la:verb:polliceor.html:
pollĭcĕor, ĭtus (
act. form polliceres, ), 2, v. dep. a. and n.
from an old prep. por or port (= Gr. πορτί, προτί, or πρός; cf. pro) and liceor
.
To hold forth, offer, promise any thing (freq. and class.; syn.: promitto, spondeo): neque minus prolixe de tuā voluntate promisi, quam eram solitus de meā polliceri,; ; cf.: alicui studium,; cf.: mirandum in modum profitentur, offerunt se, pollicentur,: id omne tibi polliceor ac defero,: pro certo polliceor hoc vobis atque confirmo me esse perfecturum, ut, etc.,: non modo ut ponatur, verum etiam ut inviolata maneat pollicetur,.—With subj. alone, : alicui divitias, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 359 Vahl.): hospitium et cenam,: plus pollicere quam ego a te postulo,.—With inf. pres.: modo Qui sum pollicitus ducere,; jusjurandum pollicitus est dare,: pollicentur obsides dare,; : benigne,: liberalissime,.—Prov.: montes auri, to promise mountains of gold, i. e. boundless wealth, ; for which also: maria montesque,.—
Esp.
Of an orator, in opening his speech, to promise, announce: quaeso ut, quid pollicitus sim, diligenter memoriae mandetis,: docui, quod primum pollicitus sum, causam omnino, cur postularet, non fuisse, etc.,.—
Of purchasers, to bid, offer: at illic pollicitus est prior,.—
Of auspices, to forebode, promise: id assuetae sanguine et praedā aves pollicebantur,.!*? Act. collat. form pollĭcĕo, ēre, to promise (ante-class.): ne dares, ne polliceres, Varr. ap. .—
polliceor, in a pass. signif.: ut aliis ob metum statuae polliceantur, Metell. Numid. ap. P.; : pollicita fides,; : pollicitus torus,.—Hence, subst.: pollĭcĭ-tum, i, n., something promised, a promise, : memores polliciti nostri,.—In plur.: hanc tu pollicitis corrumpe,: pollicitis captus,; .
la:verb:polliceor.inflection: ĭtus, v. dep. a., n., prep.

la:verb:polio.html:
pŏlĭo, īvi and ĭi, ītum, 4 (
imperf polibant, ), v. a.
root par, in parēre, appārere; cf. pulcher
, to smooth, furbish, polish (class.; syn.: limo, levigo).
Lit.: ROGVM ASCIA NE POLITO, Fragm. XII. Tab. ap. : parietem tectorio,: daedala signa,: gemmas cotibus,: ligna squatinae piscis cute,. marmora, : scabritiam ferri hircorum sanguine,: lapis politus,: polite lanceas,.—
Transf. (= apparare, curare, colere), to set off, adorn, decorate, embellish: causa poliendi agri, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 324 Vahl.); cf.: campi politi, (Sat. v. 23 Vahl.); and: politus culturā fundus,: vestes,to scour,; cf. vestimenta,; ; : linum in filo,: minium in officinis,; cf. Sillig ad : domus polita,well-ordered,; cf.: regie polita aedificia,.—
Trop., to polish, refine, improve, adorn: ignarus poliendae orationis, Cic. de Or. 1, 14, 63: ut opus poliat lima non exterat,: verba,: materiam versibus senariis,: carmina,: mores,. —Hence, pŏlītus, a, um, P. a. (in the trop. sense), polished, accomplished, refined, cultivated, polite (class.): doctrinā homines,: homo politus e scholā,: politus artibus,: homo (orator),: aliquem politum reddere,. accurata et polita oratio, ; cf.: ornata oratio et polita,; so, epistula,.—Comp.: Crassus (in dicendo) politior et ornatior,: facundia politiorem fieri,: homo politioris humanitatis expers,.—Sup.: vir omni liberali doctrinā politissimus,.—Hence, adv.: pŏlītē, in a polished manner, exquisitely, elegantly: polite subtiliterque effici,: polite apteque dicere,: ornate politeque dicere,: scribere,.—Comp.: politius perfectiusque proferre aliquid,: politius limare,.

Voc. pol, edepol, v.infra), m., = Πολυδεύκης, a famous pugilist, son of Tyndarus and Leda, and brother of Castor, in connection with whom, as the constellation of the Twins (Gemini, v. 2. Castor), he serves as a guide to mariners, ; ; ; : ita me ... Castor, Polluces ... dique omnes ament,; , 4, 27.—Poet.: geminus Pollux,i. e. Rein. cl. 1, n. 218.—In voc., contr. pol, and length. edepol (aedep-), interj. (cf.: ecastor, equirine, etc.), by Pollux! indeed! truly! pol mihi fortuna magis nunc defit quam genus, Enn. ap. (Trag. v. 394 Vahl.); id. ap. (Ann. v. 100 ib.); ; Com. Fragm. p. 67 Rib.; : per pol quam paucos reperias meretricibus fideles,: pol, me miserum, patrone, vocares,; .—In connection with other particles of affirmation: pol profecto,indeed, truly,: certe pol,: sane pol,: pol vero,.— In the form edepol: certe edepol scio,: credo edepol equidem dormire Solem,; 180.—With other particles: ne edepol,: non edepol volo profecto,: certe edepol,: immo edepol vero,.

With abl.: formā, (4, 9), 17: pecuniā,: armis,: gloriā antiquitatis,: nobilitate,: malis artibus,: gratiā,. —

To be of worth, to be valued, esteemed, : cum eadem vitis aliud aliis in locis polleat,.—

(Trag. Rel. p. 11 Rib.): equo pollens,: opibus,: venenis,.—With gen.: vini pollens Liber, (Fleck. as one word, vinipollens).—With acc.: soror cuncta pollentis viri, Argolica Juno,.—With inf.: tractare sereno Imperio vulgum pollens,; .—Hence, adv.: pollenter, powerfully (post-class.); comp. pollentius, .

la:verb:polluceo.html:
pollūcĕo, xi, ctum, 2, v. a.
old prep. port = Gr. προτί, πρός, and liceor; root licof linquo; Gr. λειπω; cf. licet

Lit., in relig. lang., to place upon the altar as a sacrifice to the deity, to offer, offer up: Jovi dapali culignam vini quantumvis polluceto ... cum pollucere oportebit, sic facies, etc.,: polluxi tibi iam publicando epulo Herculis decumas, Naev. ap. P. (Com. Rel. p. 9 Rib.): decumam partem Herculi,: pisces, Cass. Hem. ap. : pollucere merces (quas cuivis deo) liceat, sunt far, polenta, vinum, panis fermentalis, ficus passa, suilla, bubula, agnina, casei, ovilla, alica, sesama et oleum, pisces quibus est squama praeter scarum: Herculi autem omnia esculenta, potulenta, Müll.—
Transf.
To serve up as a dish: non ego sum pollucta pago, I am no dish for the village (like the Engl. saying, I am meat for your master), .—
To entertain, to treal with a thing (ante- and post-class.). *
Lit., jocosely: polluctus virgis servus,.—*
Trop., to cause to share in or partake of, .—Hence,
pol-luctum, i, n., the thing offered, an offering; also, a sacrificial banquet: polluctum quod a porricendo est fictum. Cum enim ex mercibus libamenta porrecta sunt Herculi in aram, tum polluctum est, Müll.: ad polluctum emere, Cass. Hem. ap. : polluctum Herculis,; .—
polluctē, adv., with rich offerings, sumptuously, magnificently: pollucte prodigus, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Fest. s. v. prodegeris, p. 229 Müll. (dub.).
